evidence_class: Technical review of installed V2 physical surfaces
review_scope: Installed physical composition and its existing close-up camera set.

images.observation: The fixed boiler view retains the face seams, pressure gauge and overhead pipe.
Shelf frames, floor grain and the common hall threshold remain visible behind the chair.
Tile courses meet the corner and pass behind the toilet cistern.
The fixed view remains brick-only, which limits verification of the dumbwaiter hardware.
The floor, table, central fixture and illuminated door surrounds compose under the room lighting.
The flashlight separates the tile and fabric surfaces at the bath corner.
The resident, furnishings and radiator remain visible under the ceiling fixtures.
The shelves and window trim read across the installed timber floor.
Wall sheen, counter edge and floorboards remain distinct in the hotspot.
The opened panel shows the leaf, fuse faces and conduit.
A low bench sightline shows floor tile and trim. The cat remains largely in shadow.
The portrait and orange cat on the wood shelf are visible in the low light.
The existing standing angle shows the worn painted beam and shelving beneath it.
The mail slots and door seams remain visible above the lobby bench.
The repositioned dress form sits at the left edge. The cast sections, supply wheel, and sewing table are clearly visible. A separate standing view shows both wedge working faces.
The roof landing guard, drive and access leaf are separated under the overhead light.
Tank hoops, support frame and roof brick read against the exterior sky.
The green cast, terminal case and pinned papers remain distinct.
The wall tile courses remain aligned at the corner behind the cistern.
The colored residue is bounded against the timber boards, with the radiator and both wedge faces visible behind it.
The radiator front, tendrils, and floor contact are visible. The moved dress form is clear of the mechanism at frame left.
Crumbs remain distinct on the speckled counter. The toaster and pots retain their own silhouettes.
The station trim and face remain visible on the dark textured plaster.
